messages.content:
A retry can send the same notification again

A notification is accepted by the provider, but a later retry for the same notification ID sends it again. Please trace the application path and any related delivery state, cite the relevant source from this snapshot, and explain the scope of the behavior.

candidate_links.relation: dispatch creates a fresh ledger and uses its instance-local sent set

report.summary: dispatch_notification constructs a fresh DeliveryLedger for each call. The ledger initializes an empty instance-local set, then the function checks it, sends the notification, and marks the ID only when the provider response is accepted. A later retry creates another empty ledger, so it can send the same ID again. This establishes the behavior in this dispatch path; the Run returned no upstream caller.

candidate_links.relation: dispatch creates a fresh ledger and uses its instance-local sent set

findings.text: dispatch_notification creates a new DeliveryLedger before checking was_sent; when the ID is absent it invokes sender.send(notification_id), and an accepted response triggers mark_sent.
DeliveryLedger initializes _sent_ids as a new empty set and reads/writes notification IDs only through that instance's was_sent and mark_sent methods.

candidate_links.relation: dispatch creates a fresh ledger and uses its instance-local sent set

limitations: The static neighbor result returned no upstream caller for dispatch_notification, so the established scope is this indexed dispatch path; the Run does not establish how external retry scheduling invokes it.
